dicas.texto: Which number in Chris's fraction tells how many equal parts the whole is divided into?
Look at the denominator of Chris's fraction and enter that number in the denominator field.
Chris's fraction is written as 2/8, so use the bottom number rather than the number of original pizza slices.
Type the denominator of 2/8 into the field and confirm the division.
What does the numerator tell you to count on a number line divided into equal parts?
Start at 0 and count equal intervals toward 1 using the numerator as the number of intervals.
Count two intervals from 0, while keeping the eight-part division shown on Chris's line.
Place the point at the end of the second interval and submit the fraction represented by that location.
Which part of Tracy's fraction tells how many equal sections make the whole?
Read the denominator of Tracy's fraction and enter it in the denominator field.
Tracy's fraction is 1/4, so use the bottom number as the number of equal parts.
Type the denominator of 1/4 into Tracy's field and confirm the division.
What does the numerator tell you to count from 0?
Use the four equal intervals and count forward from 0 according to the numerator.
Move one interval from 0 on Tracy's four-part number line.
Place the point at the end of the first interval and submit the fraction represented there.
Compare the positions of the two marked points on the number lines.
A point farther to the right represents a greater fraction of the pizza.
Check whether the two marked locations are different or align at the same distance from 0.
Select the statement that matches the comparison shown by the two marked points.
Have you completed both number-line markings and the comparison selection?
Review the two marked points and the selected comparison before submitting.
Make sure the final fraction comparison uses the values 2/8 and 1/4.
When every required component is complete, press the Done button to submit the activity.

exercicio.statement:
Chris and Tracy each ordered a pizza for lunch, but for some reason, Chris's pizza was divided into 6 slices, and Tracy's pizza was divided into 4 slices. Regardless, they enjoyed their lunch. Use the number line to find out which student ate more pizza.
Chris ate 2/8 of the pizza.
Tracy ate 1/4 of the pizza.
Who has eaten more pizza?
